comments.note: AvaloniaBookmarkSettingsService: videoPath is passed as null to BookmarkSettingsViewModel, so frame-nudge NudgeAsync short-circuits silently. The IBookmarkSettingsService interface does not include videoPath in its ShowAsync signature. A future WP should either add videoPath to the signature or supply it via the player context.

BookmarkSettingsViewModel.SetRatingCommand takes int parameter — XAML passes CommandParameter as string so the generated RelayCommand source generator needs to handle string-to-int conversion. If binding fails at runtime, consider using separate SetRating0..SetRating6 commands or an IValueConverter. Verify manually when the UI is exercised.

DapperBookmarkRepository was discovered missing and created by the sub-agent during this WP. This was a pre-existing gap. The repository should be audited to confirm SQL matches the movies_bookmarks table schema (m042 migration).

DapperBookmarkRepository uses fully parameterized queries throughout (no string-concatenated SQL). BookmarkSettingsViewModel applies Description.Trim() and Math.Clamp(0,6) before building the Bookmark record. Compiled AXAML x:DataType bindings prevent dynamic evaluation risks. NudgeAsync correctly uses a finally block for temp file cleanup — exemplary pattern.

INFO | A04 — Insecure Design (dead parameter) | File: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/BookmarkSettingsViewModel.cs, constructor (line 106) and BuildBookmark() (line 248). The 'hash' parameter is accepted by the full runtime constructor and stored in '_hash' but is never referenced in BuildBookmark() or any other method. It is not persisted to the Bookmark record. This means the hash is silently dropped during persistence. If the hash is required for future de-duplication or integrity checks, a silent omission from the persisted record could be a data-integrity gap. Remediation: either add 'Hash = _hash' to the new Bookmark initializer in BuildBookmark(), or explicitly document that hash is reserved for future use and not persisted yet.

SetRatingCommand is declared as RelayCommand<int> but AXAML passes CommandParameter as a string literal (e.g. CommandParameter='1'). CommunityToolkit.Mvvm RelayCommand<int> performs a direct cast, which will fail at runtime if Avalonia does not coerce the type. This must be verified manually during UI testing. If binding silently fails, consider using a dedicated SetRating0..SetRating6 set of commands or an IValueConverter. File: BookmarkSettingsView.axaml, rating buttons.

AvaloniaBookmarkSettingsService correctly uses the ownerFactory() pattern consistent with all other dialog services in Program.cs. The null-guard on owner (returns null) is correct. The CloseRequested/finally unsubscription pattern is clean and leak-free.

DapperBookmarkRepository is clean: all six SQL queries are fully parameterised via Dapper CommandDefinition anonymous objects. The two-step INSERT + SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID() reuses the same connection object, making it effectively atomic within a single session. The private BookmarkRow DTO pattern for Dapper materialisation is correct and consistent with other repositories.
